subject: qilin
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: qilin, scaled hooved chimera with antlers and cloud mane.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
Antler orientation requires immediate attention. Observed renderings show antlers projecting forward, which deviates from both mythological depictions and biological anatomy where antlers typically curve upward and backward. This discrepancy necessitates adjustment to align the antlers with a more graceful, upward sweep.


The current antler positioning uses local head coordinates, where +Y is forward and +Z is up, leading to forward-pointing antlers. Correcting this involves reorienting the antlers to sweep upwards and backwards. The chest medallion's incorrect placement arises from misaligned local coordinates.


The chest medallion positioning needs correction, placing it on the front breast between the shoulders. The hagoromo sash requires adjustment to drape more naturally. The mane's cloud features appear undersized; a larger, more voluminous design is needed. The turquoise shape on top of the head requires identification as a potential ear component, likely the skull.


The tall turquoise block appears to be the incorrectly oriented snout. Examining the frustum box calculations shows it was constructed vertically, with the "up" direction along local +Z, instead of forward. The local +Y axis, which is forward, aligns with the "up" vector of the snout, resulting in the vertical placement. The local coordinate system of the head dictates that +Y is forward and +Z is up, so the z coordinate in the `head.local()` calls correspond to the up axis.


The coordinate system uses a convention where +Y is forward and +Z is up within `head.local()`. Incorrect application of this convention resulted in the snout, antlers, and jaw being oriented incorrectly. The snout, intended to be forward, was constructed vertically, while the antlers pointed forward and slightly down. The jaw also ended up pointing upward.


The chest bone's orientation and the use of its local Z-axis caused the medallion to be placed incorrectly on the back. Further examination indicates that the flank plates, using world coordinates, are floating, suggesting they are not correctly attached to the body. Motes assigned to the wrong bones are floating in mid-air, indicating an issue with bone assignments or parenting. These combined issues explain all observed rendering anomalies. The entire module needs refactoring, with precise coordinate specifications to eliminate axis confusion.


Initial assessment of the Qilin anatomy reveals a need for detailed, organized redesign planning. Identifying and cataloging the key anatomical features, from the body and head to appendages and adornments, provides a framework for coordinating subsequent adjustments. A detailed breakdown of the required elements, informed by mythological depictions, will ensure fidelity to the envisioned aesthetic.


A dimensional framework is being established for the Qilin, including total height, body length, and skeletal coordinates using world space and local head coordinates. Correct application of `head.local({ forward, up, left, right })` with word-based directionality is confirmed to prevent coordinate system confusion. The detailed breakdown extends from overall dimensions down to specific head features, creating a coordinate system mapping to verify anatomical placements.


A frustum box has been defined for the head, with precise dimensions and tapering. The jaw's joint and frustum box are specified relative to the head. A cloud beard will attach to the jaw tip.

Eye positions are set on the skull, with an outward and forward facing direction. The antler socket is defined, along with a detailed point-based construction that specifies the sweep upward and backward. Branch points are established for brow, trez, and crown tines, completing the antler structure.


Deer-like ears, petal-shaped, are positioned behind the antlers using head-relative coordinates, with specific base and tip placements. Dragon-style whiskers are defined by a series of head-relative coordinates, with a curve originating at the snout's side.

Chest, breast, and harness components are placed using world coordinates and local direction vectors; the medallion is at the breast center. The hagoromo scarf is designed to loop under the chest, arch over the withers, billow outwards, and trail behind the hips, informed by artistic representations.


A flowing ribbon, with silk-like properties and gold borders, will be created to frame the creature in an elegant arch, including a curled tail. The mane will be redesigned as a multi-layered cloud structure, incorporating a continuous cloud ridge, overlapping spirals, cloud "wings" at the shoulders, wisps at the limbs, and a plume at the tail. The limb IK target will be verified, and the dais height checked.


The dais's dimensions and the hoof placement were verified, concluding the hoof target should be at y = 0.070 or 0.072. Each hoof will have a golden coronet with runes and cloven digits. Ankle cloud tufts will also be added.

The dais design will be a celestial lotus platform with a dark lapis base, gold trim, jade upper tier, golden rim, swirling clouds at the base, and floating spirit motes. Spirit motes will be static scenery, attached to the root joint to prevent skinning to bones.


Floating motes will be assigned based on proximity to leg bones using `b.part`, ensuring they are correctly positioned relative to the limbs. For the pedestal, static motes will be placed at the center, attached to `hips`, or explicitly attached to the pedestal, with an improved design choice of lotus lanterns or golden censers.

The Qilin's paint scheme will be refined to a more vibrant aesthetic using jade green with gold highlights for dorsal scales and a warm cream belly. Cel shading will be applied for a high-contrast anime style.

Current part and triangle counts are within budget, allowing for increased detail like cloud manes, tail plumes, and cloven hooves with rune bands.


Color palettes and textures are being established to inform the Qilin's aesthetic. A jade green scale pattern with golden dorsal scutes and cream ventral countershading has been defined. Custom textures will be generated for the eye, chest medallion, and hoof runes.


A hierarchical skeleton was constructed, defining joints for hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, and tail with relative positions. The torso was built using a loft method with four stations that specify width and height. Golden triangular crest spikes will be added along the spine.


Layered golden and jade scale plates will be applied to the flanks, extending from hips to withers. An elliptical cross-section defines the neck, which will be covered in scales. A helper function will be used to generate voluminous cloud puffs for the mane.

The mane incorporates a swept cloud crest with alternating cream and cyan puffs, large shoulder cloud mantles, and a throat cloud ruff. The skull uses a sphere scaled to specific dimensions at a defined position.

The snout uses a forward-pointing frustum box with a specific start, end, dimensions, and golden nostrils. A golden bridge plate will run along the top of the muzzle, attaching to the jaw.


Lower jaw frustum dimensions and position are being updated, along with tooth placement and a cloud chin beard. Eye placement uses head-relative coordinates and a defined outward gaze. A forehead jewel and central horn are specified with luminous properties and upward-forward direction. Antler construction utilizes a multi-point, head-relative coordinate system for a graceful upward and backward sweep, with branching brow and trez tines.


Antler crown fork points are specified with head-relative coordinates, capped with crystalline prism tips. Ear placement defines the base and tip, using head-relative coordinates, resulting in a dual-sweep design. Dragon whiskers are positioned with head-relative coordinates for graceful arching and flowing movement.

Chest components are located using world coordinates, defining the harness and medallion placement. The sash is positioned with a flow that arcs and billows, using artistic references to inform its placement.

Shoulder and hip sockets, along with hoof positions, are established using world coordinates; dais height verification also occurred. The creation of cloud treads for each hoof has been added.


Digitigrade legs with IK controls, golden armor on knees and hocks, and cloud wisps were added, along with rune-inscribed fetlocks and cloven hooves. A sinuous dragon tail with golden spines and a cloud plume, bound by a golden cuff with a tassel, was designed. The dais will be a lapis and jade lotus platform with swirling clouds, and spirit lights will be placed on lotus pedestals to avoid floating issues. The jaw will be posed open to expose fangs, and the Qilin is set for export. Coordinate logic will be reviewed, noting head.local() directionality.
